newsitem.title: USA: Three dead, other victims feared in wall collapse.
newsitem.headline: Three dead, other victims feared in wall collapse.

text.p: Three people died and as many as six others were feared dead on Thursday when a concrete wall toppled over at a shopping centre undergoing renovation, officials said.

Houston Fire Chief Eddie Corral said rescue workers had pulled three bodies from beneath "several tonnes" of debris that came crashing down when a 150-foot-long (45-metre-long) wall collapsed on a group of elderly people who were walking in the mall for exercise.
"We have identified three (bodies) ... it's a possibility of four to six (more bodies) after that," Corral told reporters gathered at Northline Mall in north Houston.
He said the possible number of other victims came from family members who had reported missing relatives and a videotape taken from a security camera at the mall.
Three large cranes were being used to pull away massive roof beams and concrete slabs that fell on the victims for reasons that were still unknown.

Sixty rescue workers crawled over the site, working under floodlights as darkness fell and using dogs and detection equipment to look for bodies. Officials said there was only a remote possibility there were survivors beneath the rubble.

Six people were injured in the wall collapse, but only one of those remained in the hospital on Thursday night with a shattered ankle, officials said. A firefighter working at the scene also suffered a leg injury, Corral said.

The collapse occurred on Thursday morning when demolition teams were tearing down a vacant department store to make way for a Magic Johnson movie theatre. The 20-foot-tall (6-metre-tall) wall enclosed a hallway next to the store.
One witness, Carol Nunez, said the wall may have been knocked over by demolition equipment.
"They were picking at the building with one of their tractors and then the next thing you know the whole thing just came down," Nunez said. "It was like a row of dominos falling over."
Mayor Bob Lanier, who toured the scene, said the city was investigating the cause of the collapse but it was too early to speculate on what had happened.
One of the injured, Elizabeth Lingold, told a local television station that she and her husband were walking in the hallway next to the wall when it began to cave in.
"We heard this kind of boom ... something was falling and (my husband) pushed me and said 'run'. I ran, but I looked back over my shoulder and it was just like waves coming down," she said.
Lingold said the falling wall created a blast of air so powerful she and her husband were lifted from their feet and thrown clear of the collapsing rubble.

"We were not lucky, we were blessed," she said. Many elderly people, who call themselves "mall walkers," use shopping malls as an exercise place because the malls are considered safer than the streets.
